comments.text:
The information in this video is misleading. And by looking at other comments here looks like every one was easily misled as well. Not to blame as most including the video creator are not technically skilled to understand how digital signing works. That option that he disabled is enabled by defualt in Acrobat reader for a reason, as it is important to verify if the signature in the PDF is truly valid or not. That option ensures that the software verifies whether the certificate used to sign a document has been revoked. If this check is disabled, Adobe Reader will not verify the current trustworthiness of the certificate, which could allow for the acceptance of signatures from revoked or untrustworthy certificates.

And if you save a print-pdf version of this document as one of the top comments here suggested, then you completely let go of the digital signature data embedded in this document, all you see in that print-pdf is the visual representation of the verified signature. It is not the actual signature that can veirify author's identity.
